records.text: The seventh month arrived—the sons of Israel being in their cities—and the people gathered as one man in Jerusalem.

Iesous son of Iosedek and his brothers the priests, and Zorobabel son of Salathiel and his brothers, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer whole burnt offerings upon it according to what is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
They prepared the altar on its prepared place, for terror from the peoples of the lands was upon them. A whole burnt offering went up upon it to the Lord, in the morning and toward evening.
They kept the Festival of Booths according to what was written, with whole burnt offerings day by day in the number required by the ordinance, each day’s due on its own day,
and afterward continual whole burnt offerings, those for the new moons and all the consecrated festivals, and for everyone freely presenting a freewill offering to the Lord.

They gave silver to the stonecutters and craftsmen, and food, drink and oil to the Sedanin and Sorin, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the concession of Cyrus king of the Persians to them.

They answered in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord: “For it is good, for His mercy toward Israel endures for ever.” All the people sounded a great cry of praise to the Lord at the founding of the Lord’s house.

Many of the priests and Levites and leaders of the families—the elders who had seen the first house at its founding, and who saw this house before their eyes—wept with a loud voice; and the multitude cried aloud with joy to raise a song.
The two companies of praise stood in God’s house, with me and half the commanders with me,
and the priests Eliakim, Maasias, Beniamin, Michaias, Elioenai, Zacharias and Ananias with trumpets,
and Maasias, Semeias, Eleazar, Ozi, Joanan, Melchias, Ailam and Ezour. The singers were heard and were appointed.
In the reign of Asoueros, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote a letter against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
Raoum the baaltam and Samsai the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to Arthasastha the king.

These things were decided by Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe and the rest of our fellow slaves—the Dinaians, Apharsathachaians, Tarphallaians, Apharsaians, Archyaians, Babylonians and Sousanachaians, who are Elamites,
and the remaining nations whom the great and honored Asennaphar had deported and settled in the cities of Somoron, and the remainder beyond the river.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, the king fell into visions and dreams and was disturbed in his dream, and his sleep left him.
The king ordered the incantation-singers, magi, and sorcerers of the Chaldeans brought in to report his dreams to him. They arrived and stood beside the king.
The king said to them, “I have seen a dream, and my spirit was stirred; therefore I wish to understand the dream.”

The king answered the Chaldeans, “Unless you truthfully report the dream to me and disclose its interpretation, you will be made a public example, and your possessions will be taken into the royal treasury.
The king said, “Who is this who dared to do this deed?”
Esther said, “An enemy—this wicked Haman!” Haman was disturbed before the king and the queen.
The king rose from the banquet and went into the garden. Haman pleaded with the queen, for he saw that he himself was in trouble.

The king returned from the garden, and Haman had fallen upon the couch, entreating the queen. The king said, “Are you even forcing yourself on the woman in my house?” When Haman heard this, his face changed.
This is the account of the decree that Arthasastha gave Esdras the priest, the scribe of the book of the words of the Lord’s commandments and His ordinances for Israel:
“Arthasastha, king of kings, to Esdras, scribe of the law of the God of heaven: The word and the answer are completed.
I have issued a decision that anyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel, the priests and the Levites who freely wishes to go to Jerusalem is to go with you.
and, for the Lord’s house, silver and gold that the king and the advisers have freely offered to the God of Israel who dwells in Jerusalem,
and all the silver and gold you may find throughout the country of Babylon, with the voluntary offering of the people and priests who freely offer for the house of God in Jerusalem,

and everything that comes in—readily enter this in this book: young bulls, rams, lambs, their sacrifices and their drink offerings. You shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
Whatever seems good to you and your brothers to do with the remaining silver and gold, do as is pleasing to your God.
The vessels given to you for the service of God’s house, hand over before God in Jerusalem.
Whatever else you think your God’s house needs, you shall provide from the king’s treasury houses.
I, Arthasastha the king, have issued a decision to all the treasuries beyond the river: whatever Esdras the priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven asks of you, let it be provided readily,
up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred kors of wheat, one hundred bads of wine, one hundred bads of oil, and salt for which there is no written amount.
Let everything in the decision of the God of heaven be done. Take care that no one attempts anything against the house of the God of heaven, lest wrath come upon the kingdom of the king and his sons.

You, Esdras, according to the wisdom of God in your hand, appoint scribes and judges to judge all the people beyond the river, all who know the law of your God; and you shall make it known to the one who does not know.
For anyone who does not readily carry out the law of God and the law of the king, judgment shall be executed against him, whether death, discipline, loss of property, or bonds.”
But Queen Astin did not obey his command to come with the eunuchs. The king was grieved and became angry.
He said to his friends, “Astin has spoken in this way; therefore establish law and judgment concerning this.”
Arcesaeus, Sarsathaeus, and Malesehar, the rulers of Persia and Media who were nearest the king and sat in the first places beside him, approached him
and reported to him, according to the laws, how Queen Astin must be dealt with, because she had not done what the king commanded through the eunuchs.
And Joseph bought all the land of the Egyptians for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharaoh, because the famine prevailed over them. And the land became Pharaoh’s.
And he enslaved the people to him as slaves, from one end of the borders of Egypt to the other.

At the dedication of Jerusalem’s wall, they sought the Levites in their places to bring them to Jerusalem, to celebrate the dedication and gladness with thodatha and songs, sounding cymbals, with psalteries and lyres.
The sons of the singers gathered from the surrounding district to Jerusalem and from farmsteads,
and from fields, for the singers had built farmsteads for themselves in Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites were purified, and they purified the people, the gatekeepers and the wall.
I brought the rulers of Jouda up onto the wall and stationed two great ones for praise. They went along to the right on top of the wall of refuse,
